q-162231.name: Question 1
q-162231.problem: Calculate the circulation $Γ$ of the vector field $F(x,y,z)=x\,i-z\,j+y\,k$ along the closed curve $C$ given by $r(t)=2\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\,j+\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\,k$ for $t\in [0,2).$
q-162231.worked_solution:
The circulation $Γ$ measures the total work done by a force $F$ in moving a particle along a *closed* curve $C.$
It is given by the formula

$$
Γ={∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=2,\,y=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t),\,z=\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t).
$$

So,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =x\,i-z\,j+y\,k \\  & =2\,i-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\,j+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t))\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t))\,k \\  & =0\,i-\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\,j+\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(2\,i-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\,j+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\,k)\cdot (-\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\,j+\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\,k) \\  & =2\cdot 0+(-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t))\cdot (-\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t))+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\cdot \pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t) \\  & =\pi {sin}^{2}⁡(\pi t)+\pi {cos}^{2}⁡(\pi t) \\  & =\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Γ={∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{2}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\pi \,\text{d}t \\  & =\pi [t]_{0}^{2} \\  & =\pi (2-0) \\  & =2\pi \end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

Calculate the circulation Γ of the vector field F(x,y,z)=xi−zj+yk along the closed curve C given by r(t)=2i+cos⁡(πt)j+sin⁡(πt)k for t∈[0,2).

a
2π
b
π
c
1
d
0
e
2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The circulation Γ measures the total work done by a force F in moving a particle along a closed curve C. It is given by the formula Γ=∮CF⋅dr=∫abF(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt.

Along the curve C, we have x=2,y=cos⁡(πt),z=sin⁡(πt).

So,

F(r(t))=xi−zj+yk=2i−sin⁡(πt)j+cos⁡(πt)k.

Computing r′(t), we get

r′(t)=ddt(2)i+ddt(cos⁡(πt))j+ddt(sin⁡(πt))k=0i−πsin⁡(πt)j+πcos⁡(πt)k.

Therefore,

F(r(t))⋅r′(t)=(2i−sin⁡(πt)j+cos⁡(πt)k)⋅(−πsin⁡(πt)j+πcos⁡(πt)k)=2⋅0+(−sin⁡(πt))⋅(−πsin⁡(πt))+cos⁡(πt)⋅πcos⁡(πt)=πsin2⁡(πt)+πcos2⁡(πt)=π.

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

Γ=∮CF⋅dr=∫02F(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt=∫02πdt=π[t]02=π(2−0)=2π

q-162229.name: Question 2
q-162229.problem: Calculate the circulation $Γ$ of the vector field $F(x,y,z)=-y\,i+x\,j$ along the closed curve $C$ given by $r(t)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\,j+2\,k$ for $t\in [0,2).$
q-162229.worked_solution:
The circulation $Γ$ measures the total work done by a force $F$ in moving a particle along a *closed* curve $C.$
It is given by the formula

$$
Γ={∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t),\,y=\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t),\,z=2.
$$

So,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =-y\,i+x\,j \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\,i+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t))\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t))\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2)\,k \\  & =-2\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\,i+\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\,j+0\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\,i+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\,j)\cdot (-2\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\,i+\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\,j+0\,k) \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\cdot (-2\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t))+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\cdot \pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)+0\cdot 0 \\  & =2\pi {sin}^{2}⁡(\pi t)+2\pi {cos}^{2}⁡(\pi t) \\  & =2\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Γ={∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{2}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}2\pi \,\text{d}t \\  & =2\pi [t]_{0}^{2} \\  & =2\pi (2-0) \\  & =4\pi \end{aligned}
$$

q-162238.name: Question 3
q-162238.problem: Calculate the circulation $Γ$ of the vector field $F(x,y,z)=(y-x)\,i$ along the closed curve $C$ given by $r(t)=({t}^{2}-t)\,i+({t}^{3}-t)\,j+\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi t)\,k$ for $t\in [0,1).$
q-162238.worked_solution:
The circulation $Γ$ measures the total work done by a force $F$ in moving a particle along a *closed* curve $C.$
It is given by the formula

$$
Γ={∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x={t}^{2}-t,\,y={t}^{3}-t,\,z=\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi t).
$$

So,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =(y-x)\,i \\  & =({t}^{3}-t-{t}^{2}+t)\,i \\  & =({t}^{3}-{t}^{2})\,i.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}-t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi t)\,)\,k \\  & =(2t-1)\,i+(3{t}^{2}-1)\,j+2\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi t)\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(\,({t}^{3}-{t}^{2})\,i\,)\cdot (\,(2t-1)\,i+(3{t}^{2}-1)\,j+2\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi t)\,k\,) \\  & =({t}^{3}-{t}^{2})\cdot (2t-1)+0\cdot (3{t}^{2}-1)+0\cdot 2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi t) \\  & =2{t}^{4}-{t}^{3}-2{t}^{3}+{t}^{2} \\  & =2{t}^{4}-3{t}^{3}+{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

  

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Γ={∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{1}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(\,2{t}^{4}-3{t}^{3}+{t}^{2}\,)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={[\frac{2{t}^{5}}{5}-\frac{3{t}^{4}}{4}+\frac{{t}^{3}}{3}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(\frac{2}{5}-\frac{3}{4}+\frac{1}{3})-(0) \\  & =-\frac{1}{60}\end{aligned}
$$

The circulation Γ measures the total work done by a force F in moving a particle along a closed curve C. It is given by the formula Γ=∮CF⋅dr=∫abF(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt.

So,

F(r(t))=(y−x)i=(t3−t−t2+t)i=(t3−t2)i.

r′(t)=ddt(t2−t)i+ddt(t3−t)j+ddt(sin⁡(2πt))k=(2t−1)i+(3t2−1)j+2πcos⁡(2πt)k.

F(r(t))⋅r′(t)=((t3−t2)i)⋅((2t−1)i+(3t2−1)j+2πcos⁡(2πt)k)=(t3−t2)⋅(2t−1)+0⋅(3t2−1)+0⋅2cos⁡(2πt)=2t4−t3−2t3+t2=2t4−3t3+t2.

Γ=∮CF⋅dr=∫01F(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt=∫01(2t4−3t3+t2)dt=[2t55−3t44+t33]01=(25−34+13)−(0)=−160

q-162232.problem: Calculate the circulation $Γ$ of the vector field $F(x,y,z)=x\,i-z\,k$ along the closed curve $C$ given by $r(t)=({t}^{2}-t)\,i+({t}^{3}-{t}^{2})\,j+k$ for $t\in [0,1).$
q-162232.worked_solution:
The circulation $Γ$ measures the total work done by a force $F$ in moving a particle along a *closed* curve $C.$
It is given by the formula

$$
Γ={∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x={t}^{2}-t,\,y={t}^{3}-{t}^{2},\,z=1.
$$

So,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =x\,i-z\,k \\  & =({t}^{2}-t)\,i-1\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}-{t}^{2})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)\,k \\  & =(2t-1)\,i+(3{t}^{2}-2t)\,j+0\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(({t}^{2}-t)\,i-\,k)\cdot ((2t-1)\,i+(3{t}^{2}-2t)\,j) \\  & =({t}^{2}-t)\cdot (2t-1)+0\cdot (3{t}^{2}-2t)+(-1)\cdot 0 \\  & =({t}^{2}-t)(2t-1).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Γ={∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{1}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}({t}^{2}-t)(2t-1)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={[\frac{({t}^{2}-t)^{2}}{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(0-0) \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

The circulation Γ measures the total work done by a force F in moving a particle along a closed curve C. It is given by the formula Γ=∮CF⋅dr=∫abF(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt.

Along the curve C, we have x=t2−t,y=t3−t2,z=1.

So,

F(r(t))=xi−zk=(t2−t)i−1k.

Computing r′(t), we get

r′(t)=ddt(t2−t)i+ddt(t3−t2)j+ddt(1)k=(2t−1)i+(3t2−2t)j+0k.

Therefore,

F(r(t))⋅r′(t)=((t2−t)i−k)⋅((2t−1)i+(3t2−2t)j)=(t2−t)⋅(2t−1)+0⋅(3t2−2t)+(−1)⋅0=(t2−t)(2t−1).

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

Γ=∮CF⋅dr=∫01F(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt=∫01(t2−t)(2t−1)dt=[(t2−t)22]01=(0−0)=0
